title: No command reports which linked worktrees are landed, so they pile up: a read-only report (landed, held or unknown, with evidence) and a remove-landed form (decision 72)
body:
hv ruled on 2026-10-26 (vc decision 72) that a tool to list and remove landed worktrees goes in devbin, as an issue for devbin's next release, so that every estate gets it. Intent adds only the fold text: Intent 26d8e1f39, issue 0656, on hv's Intent decision 94, "Text in Intent now, tool in devbin". intent-vc's reading is the spec, and its two inventory scripts are the measure. hv said go on filing on 2026-10-27 (vc decision 78).

Why landed worktrees pile up, from intent-vc's reading of 2026-10-26, measured in Intent's estate:
- Every unit is built and banked in its own linked worktree, and each re-bank on a new base gets another. Each worktree builds its own target, because a shared target bakes in the other tree's path.
- The worktree is held on purpose until its landing.
- Nothing ends that hold after the landing. The landing reads the bank's blob, not the worktree. A fold archives board items only, and no verb lists the worktrees whose work main already holds.
- Removing one by hand is risky. A session standing in it loses its working directory, and `--force` destroys unlanded work when the measure is wrong.
So Intent's tmp/ fills with worktrees whose work is already on main, many carrying their own Rust target.

## The contract it mechanises

in-whiteboard's Folding section, at Intent 26d8e1f39 (issue 0656):
- A landed unit's worktree is removed by its author, at the chain END that lands it, or at the author's next fold.
- Four checks run first, from outside the worktree, and hold whether its banks are staged or committed:
  - its index tree is its base with its landed banks applied;
  - nothing in it is unstaged or untracked;
  - its base is an ancestor of main;
  - no stash entry names it.
- Then `git -C <path> reset --hard` drops a bank that is still staged, and a plain `git worktree remove <path>` runs, never `--force`. A refusal is read as a finding.
- A build target linked in from another tree is removed as the link alone, with a plain `rm`.
- A mutant kept for a red run goes with its unit, once that run's END is on the record.
- A re-bank that supersedes a worktree removes the old one.

## The spec and the measure

Copied into ~/Devel/scratch/devbin-vc/wt-tool/, each file's sha256 as intent-vc gave it, and each also held in Intent's repository under refs/bank/vc/tools/:
- wt-reading.txt (0cf1f9765cb41bfe), the reading;
- inventory.sh (c78ed2249ca3e80e) and its output from Intent's estate at main 629ce5ad2, inventory.txt (829121cce6237d2f);
- pass2.sh (04d7a0e3548c3c93) and its output at main c1741b1d8, wt-pass2.out (daa147d10019f95b).
Both are read-only zsh with Intent's paths written in. Every git read takes `--no-optional-locks`, and inventory's landed test applies the diff in a scratch index of main's HEAD.

What neither script decides, from intent-vc on 2026-10-27, each with a case in Intent's estate:
1. A staged diff that is a bank's but not main's. Only the unit's board says whether that bank is live or superseded.
2. A staged diff that matches no bank and no main commit. It could be a mutant, work landed with edits, or unbanked work.
3. Own commits that read "not on main" on a scratch stack whose banks landed with different hunks, eg vc's CHANGELOG lines added at landing.
4. Landed content left unstaged. By the contract's letter that is held.
5. Untracked files. Real unlanded work and a build target linked from another tree read alike as a count.
6. A worktree kept for future use, eg vc's judge worktree, which reads as landed.
7. A process inside it. A live session and a stale shell read alike.
8. A stash entry naming it. Neither script reads `git stash list`, the contract's fourth check.
9. Plain directories under the worktree root that git does not list.
10. The two landed tests answer different questions. Reverse-applying in main's index asks whether main holds the content; a patch-id match asks whether a commit or bank is the same change. A unit landed with edits can pass the first and fail the second.
For cases 1 to 7, the honest answer is "unknown, with the evidence", and the author's word decides.

## Fix

A devbin command (eg `worktrees`, or as the design settles), read-only unless asked to remove.

- **The report:** one row per linked worktree of the repository, with its verdict and its evidence. The evidence is:
  - its HEAD, and whether main contains it;
  - its own commits not on main, by patch-id (`git cherry`);
  - its staged diff's patch-id, and whether main or a bank has it;
  - whether main already holds the staged content, by reverse-apply in a scratch index (both landed tests, per case 10);
  - unstaged and untracked files;
  - stash entries naming it (case 8);
  - any process whose working directory is inside it;
  - its index's last write.
- **The verdicts:**
  - **landed** only when the contract's four checks hold, provably;
  - **held** when a check fails over content that is not landed;
  - **unknown**, with its evidence, for cases 1 to 7.
- **Plain directories** under the worktree root that git does not list are reported with their size and no verdict (case 9).
- **A remove-landed form** removes only the rows reported landed, each by the contract's steps: `reset --hard` to drop a staged bank, then a plain `git worktree remove`, never `--force`; a linked build target goes as the link alone. It refuses any worktree with untracked files, unlanded changes, a stash entry or a process standing in it. It never runs from inside a worktree it would remove. A refusal by git is reported as a finding, never forced.
- **Generic:** the bank refs (Intent's `refs/bank/*`) are a config key, and a project with none tests against main alone. No path of Intent's is written in.

## Done when

1. On fixture repositories, the report gives each of these its verdict and evidence:
   - a worktree whose staged bank main holds (landed);
   - one with unlanded staged work (held);
   - one with untracked files;
   - one with a stash entry;
   - one with a process standing in it;
   - one whose staged diff is a bank's but not main's (unknown, case 1);
   - one whose staged diff matches neither (unknown, case 2);
   - one whose own commits read "not on main" though their content landed (case 3, both landed tests shown);
   - one with landed content left unstaged (case 4).
2. Plain directories git does not list are reported with their size and no verdict.
3. remove-landed removes exactly the landed rows, by the contract's steps and never with `--force`, and refuses each of the others, naming why.
4. Run read-only on Intent's estate beside intent-vc's two scripts, at the same main, its evidence agrees with theirs for every worktree both cover, or the Resolution explains each difference. remove-landed is not run there.
5. Its help page documents it, the landing suite passes under BSD and GNU with the tree scans and help, and CI is green on the pushed head.

## Resolution

Fixed at 7565e2a2bfa5541c16f9f9a1837a15089726483e, landed on main by vc with the rest of C (fb66b479..7565e2a2) on hv's GO of 29 Oct, as cc banked it. `worktrees [report] [--repo <dir>] [<path>...]` prints one block per linked worktree of the repository, or only the ones named, with its verdict (landed, held or unknown), every reason found and its evidence, and writes nothing. `worktrees remove-landed <path>...` removes each named worktree that reads landed, by the contract's steps, and refuses every other, naming why.

- **An always-offered builtin,** lib/cmd/worktrees, its catalogue row under Build beside clean (lib/builtins), offered in every project and refusing outside a git checkout at exit 2, under contract.bats' `# code-2:` marker. The list is read from `git worktree list --porcelain -z` in the repository the worktrees share, so it answers the same from the main worktree or a linked one.
- **The evidence,** per worktree: its HEAD and whether the branch holds it (commit_direction); its base; its own commits by `git cherry`; its staged and unstaged diffs, each under both landed tests (case 10): the change test, by `patch-id --stable` against the branch's commits from the worktree's base to its tip and against every bank, and the content test, by reverse-apply and then apply in a scratch index of the branch's tree; untracked files and linked build targets; ignored files with their size and no reason, since a plain worktree remove deletes them; stash entries naming it; processes standing in it (lsof, else /proc, the report's own processes left out); its lock and reason; and its index's last write. A prunable worktree names `git worktree prune`.
- **Plain directories** beside the worktrees, below the project root and never the root itself, are reported with their size and no verdict (vc's limit on Q6).
- **The verdicts,** as the page states them: landed only when every check holds; held when a check fails over content the branch lacks; unknown, with the evidence, where only the author can say. vc's rulings:
  - (a) staged work no commit and no bank carries reads held when the branch lacks its content, and unknown when the branch holds it;
  - (b) a stash is matched by branch name, or, for a detached worktree, by a stash made detached whose first parent is its HEAD, so two detached worktrees at one HEAD both read held: the safe failure, since a held worktree is only left standing;
  - (c) `--repo` naming a directory that is no git checkout is an operand error, exit 1; a project root that is no checkout is exit 2;
  - (d) worktrees.banks patterns are read as `git for-each-ref` reads them: `refs/bank` matches every ref beneath it at any depth, `refs/bank/*` one level only. Done when 4's config names `refs/bank`.
- **remove-landed** reads each named path again, never from an earlier report, and refuses the main worktree, a path that is no linked worktree, a gone or locked one, one the caller stands in, one the run itself stands in (the repository, the project or the devbin runtime it runs from), and anything not landed. Then it removes a linked target's link alone with `rm --`, drops a staged diff the branch holds with `reset --hard`, and runs a plain `git worktree remove`, never `--force`, reporting git's refusal as a finding. There is no bulk form: each worktree is removed by its author, who names it (Q1). A kept worktree is one locked with `git worktree lock --reason` (Q4).
- **`--repo <dir>`** (R1) reads another repository with this project's keys, for report alone; remove-landed refuses it.
- **Read-only throughout** (R2). Every read goes through git_readonly or git_readonly_index (lib/helpers), which sets GIT_INDEX_FILE to a scratch index under the same clearing and flags, both through one `_git_readonly_exec`. `git diff` from the index to the working tree writes a stat-stale index back under `--no-optional-locks` (git 2.56, measured), so each worktree's index is read through a scratch copy made with `cp -p`, since a copy stamped now defeated git's racy-entry check.
- **One scratch helper** (Q9): `scratch_outside` in lib/helpers is release_scratch's outside-the-project check and mktemp, which release_scratch (lib/release.steps) and worktrees both call.
- **The keys:** worktrees.branch (default `main`, read as `refs/heads/<branch>`, a branch the repository lacks refused naming the key) and worktrees.banks (no default, so a project with none tests against the branch alone). No path of Intent's is written in.

The critic-shell review ran once the code and arms were written, and its four warnings were settled before the first START:
- W1: every diff, `log -p` and apply goes through `_wt_diff` with one set of flags (`--no-ext-diff --no-textconv --no-color --no-relative`, git's `a/` and `b/` prefixes, `--whitespace=nowarn` on apply), and GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF and GIT_DIFF_OPTS are unset, so the wrapper is immune to diff config: under `diff.external=true` a staged diff had printed nothing, and unlanded work read landed;
- W2: remove-landed refuses removing the tree it runs from, since a launcher inside the worktree removed its own tree;
- W3: the scratch is checked against every worktree the list names once it is read, not the project alone, since from a linked worktree's project a TMPDIR inside the main worktree passed;
- W4: mtime_epoch, BSD's stat or GNU's, is hoisted from bin/.devbin/cmd/fleet into lib/helpers, and fleet calls it, as worktrees does for the index's last write.

The string comparison of a worktree's path with git's record, at lib/cmd/worktrees's index lookup, holds because git 2.56 records a worktree's path as its realpath at `worktree add`, and our side is read with physical_dir's getcwd form, so both sides are physical. Measured with a worktree added through a symlink and one added as `../rel/../rel2`, each listed resolved.

Documented in lib/pages/worktrees.md, docs/configuration.md and lib/config.reference.yaml; README.md's Always offered table gains worktrees.

- **Done when 1.** worktrees.bats gives each state its verdict and evidence: landed, "a staged bank the branch holds reads landed, with both landed tests shown (0245)" and "a staged diff a bank has, whose content the branch holds, reads landed (0245)"; held, "unlanded staged work that no commit and no bank carries reads held (0245)", with ruling (a)'s other half in "a staged diff of content main holds, that no commit and no bank carries, reads unknown (0245)"; untracked, "untracked files read unknown, each named (0245)"; a stash, "a stash entry naming a worktree reads held, naming the entry, after its HEAD has moved on (0245)" and, for ruling (b), "a stash made detached names the detached worktrees at its first parent, each reading held (0245)"; a process, "a process standing in a worktree reads unknown, naming its pid (0245)", "the report leaves out its own processes when it is run from inside a worktree (0245)" and "a process check that cannot tell reads unknown, and remove-landed refuses it (0245)"; case 1, "a staged diff a bank has and the branch lacks reads unknown, naming the bank (0245)"; case 2, "a staged diff no commit and no bank carries, landed with edits, reads unknown (0245)"; case 3, "own commits that read not on main by patch-id, though main holds their content, read unknown with both tests shown (0245)"; and case 4, "landed content left unstaged reads unknown (0245)". Beside them: "a build target linked in from another tree reads landed and is listed as a link (0245)", "a locked worktree shows its lock and reason, and remove-landed refuses it, removing nothing (0245)", "a worktree whose directory is gone reads prunable, naming git worktree prune, and remove-landed refuses it as not a directory (0245)", "a bank pattern ending in a glob matches a bank one level down and not a deeper one, as git for-each-ref does (0245)" for ruling (d), "a diff is read as git's own whatever diff.external or GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF names, so unlanded work never reads landed (0245)" for W1, "the summary counts each verdict as the blocks give it (0245)", "worktrees.branch names the branch landed work reaches, and one the repository lacks is refused naming the key (0245)", "report --repo reads another repository as that repository's own report reads it (0245)", "report --repo naming a directory that is no git checkout is refused, exit 1 (0245)" and "worktrees outside a git checkout is not available here, exit 2 (0245)" for ruling (c), and "the report writes nothing under the repository's git directory, a stale index's included (0245)".
- **Done when 2.** "plain directories beside the worktrees are reported with their size and no verdict (0245)", and "a worktree made directly in the project root lists none of the project's own directories as plain (0245)" for vc's limit on Q6.
- **Done when 3.** "remove-landed removes exactly the landed worktrees, by reset and a plain worktree remove, and refuses each other naming why (0245)" removes the landed rows and refuses the rest, reading git's state after. Each refusal has its arm, git's state read after it: "remove-landed refuses a worktree a stash names and one a process stands in, and git's state is as it was (0245)"; "remove-landed reports git's refusal of worktree remove as a finding, and forces nothing (0245)"; "remove-landed refuses a worktree the run itself stands in, its devbin runtime inside it, and removes nothing (0245)" for W2; "remove-landed refuses a worktree the caller stands in, and removes nothing (0245)"; "remove-landed refuses the main worktree and a path that is no linked worktree (0245)"; "remove-landed refuses --repo, and removes nothing (0245)"; and "a TMPDIR inside the main worktree is refused when the run is a linked worktree's own, and nothing is left there (0245)" for W3. Done when 1's locked, prunable and cannot-tell arms hold those refusals too.
- **Done when 4.** Run read-only on Intent's estate by ~/Devel/scratch/devbin-cc/0245/dw4.sh, from a scratch project vendoring 0245's build 51cbed7d by path, its config naming `worktrees.banks: [refs/bank]`, as `worktrees report --repo ~/Devel/prj/Intent`, beside copies of intent-vc's inventory.sh and pass2.sh (checked against intent-vc's SHA256SUMS first), all at Intent main d41658e7, which read the same at the start and the end: on 2026-10-28 from 06:52Z to 06:53Z, each exit 0, every git read with GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 (0245/dw4/). 51cbed7d is the change that landed as 7565e2a2; 4d1a76b0 later changed only the lsof field, which macOS's lsof writes unasked. The two agree on both linked worktrees they cover: tmp/wt-vc-train reads landed, its staged change (patch-id 47e139be9fb3) the bank refs/bank/ic/0086/pipeline-stack-v1's and in main, as the inventory reads it; tmp/wt-cc-ra reads unknown, its staged change (00c89d2767fb) the bank refs/bank/cc/ra-target/v2's, which main does not hold, as the inventory reads its staged change not in main. The report adds the nine plain directories git does not list, with their sizes. The run's seal, dw4/SHA256SUMS, was taken before dw4.sh wrote its last log line, so its dw4.log sum is the log's first five lines'; dw4/SHA256SUMS.corrected-20261029 seals the whole log beside it, its other six sums the same, and the original is kept. remove-landed was not run there.
- **Done when 5.** lib/pages/worktrees.md documents the command and its keys, docs/configuration.md and lib/config.reference.yaml the keys. surfaces.bats's "every built-in devbin ships with no options answers all for itself, and none writes anything (0128)" gains worktrees's row, exit 2 outside a checkout; help.bats's "every built-in answers with devbin's shipped page or an honest stub, and the two cover the catalogue (0113)" and "a shipped page names no docs/, intent/, tests/, lib/ or .lib/ path, no shell-gate and no unqualified issue number (0113)" read the new page; and documentation.bats's "the README's offered tables are what a freshly seeded project's help lists, and its language table what each language adds (0256)" holds README's Always offered table to the new row. The landing suite: 0245's stage of C never ran, since C was stopped on hv's word before it, so no red leg ran for 0245's arms. hv's test all at 217adf65 passed 0245's arms on macOS. K0116 on kovacs at 217adf65 (seal 20261029-0832) failed worktrees.bats 2734, 2737, 2744, 2745, 2750, 2756, 2757 and 2758: kovacs's lsof 4.99.4 writes only the fields asked for, and the process check asked for no f field, so no directory was read and every state came out unknown. 4d1a76b0 asks for -F pRcfn, which macOS's lsof 4.91 answers alike. hv's `dvb test all` on rhadamanth at 217adf65 ran every one of the 2777 tests bats counts in tests/unit once, and none failed (tmp/test/20261029-0817.bats.out, its .errors empty). K0116B, the full suite on kovacs at 4d1a76b0 with rustup's cargo first on PATH, as on CI's Ubuntu runner, is green, as vc read its seal. CI run 40851772728 on 4d1a76b0 and CI run 40860048152 on 25175386, the head 0.1.16 was cut from, are green on Test on Ubuntu, Shell Script Analysis and Test Summary. No critic leg ran on the landed commits.

- **CI:** run 40860048152 on the pushed head 25175386, which carries the landing, read green by vc.
